statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail 24 reflects extreme Gulf and rates stress while NQ is closed and no live one-way price path is observable.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: WATCH. The 22:00 UTC Globex reopening remains the next direct price-path checkpoint.
headline: Nasdaq Tail remains WATCH 24 ahead of Sunday Globex reopening
body: NQ is closed. Gulf equities finished mixed, the U.S. denied Iran's disputed vessel-strike claim, OPEC+ kept October output policy unchanged, and Friday's strong-jobs yield repricing remains unresolved. Fresh shared context is mixed and latest-session only, so it does not establish live Nasdaq persistence.

lookbackSummary: 18:00 UTC Saturday-17:00 UTC Sunday: Tail remained WATCH, eased to 21-23 in several overnight hours, then returned to 24 as Gulf escalation risk persisted while NQ stayed closed.
outlookSummary: Tail remains below blocking levels while NQ is closed. Conditional Tail reaches 34 at the 22:00 UTC reopening only if a directional gap resists repair with shallow or failed retracements and reinforcing oil/yield pressure; holiday-thin liquidity can amplify noise without proving persistent Tail.

forecast.analysis: Tail 33 persists only if the first post-open hour extends after weak retracements; meaningful two-sided repair invalidates the elevated path.
Tail 31 requires the opening direction to remain efficient with failed retracements and confirming oil or yield pressure.
Tail stays elevated only if one-way structure survives several hours; normal retracements or cross-asset stabilization weaken it.
Without repeated extension, the base path returns to WATCH; holiday-thin liquidity can create noise without proving one-way persistence.
If Asia-hours trade becomes two-sided, Tail eases while Gulf headlines and oil keep Stress high.
If the opening gap is substantially repaired, a mixed regime becomes more likely despite residual geopolitical and rates risk.
Late Asia remains WATCH if retracements are available and no new catalyst aligns oil, yields and index direction.
A balanced overnight range supports WATCH ahead of Europe; a new geopolitical discontinuity would invalidate that assumption.
At the European open, Tail can firm if oil, yields and equity futures align; directional efficiency is still required for elevation.
Europe's first hour stays WATCH unless cross-asset alignment becomes persistent; fading oil pressure would weaken the Tail case.
If Europe absorbs weekend risk without sustained extension, Tail eases; the U.S. cash-market holiday removes a major confirmation window.
At European midday, absent renewed one-way extension, holiday spikes remain Stress evidence rather than Tail evidence.
drivers: Isolated holiday spikes mainly affect Stress

forecast.analysis: If oil and yields stop reinforcing the same direction, Tail stays low-WATCH; fresh escalation could reopen the danger window.
Early U.S. holiday hours lack cash-equity confirmation; without persistent futures extension, Tail remains contained.
At the usual U.S. open window, futures-only holiday trading can swing sharply, but repeated failed retracements remain the Tail test.
drivers: Failed retracements remain the Tail test

forecast.analysis: If futures remain two-sided after the usual open window, Tail stays WATCH; an aligned oil/yield surge would be the main escalation path.
Without a U.S. cash session, sustained directional confirmation is harder; mean-reverting futures keep Tail contained.
Late holiday trading can amplify whipsaw risk; Tail rises materially only if repeated extension follows failed repair.
In the final forecast hour, two-sided trading and no fresh geopolitical shock keep Tail contained.
